summary: Create and list disk images and extract files from them
description: Works with the formats D64 (1541), D71 (1571), D81 (1581) and ATR (Atari, DOS 2). When you create an image, the subcommand sets its type. When you list or extract, the file extension sets it.
With `--add`, the first colon separates the file from the disk name. A path with a drive letter (C:\...) therefore cannot be combined with a name. Use relative paths in that case.

forms.summary: Create a D64 image (1541) with programs

options.help: Output file of the image.
Disk name in the directory header.
Disk ID in the directory header.
Write a program file (PRG) to the disk, optionally under a different name.
options.default_text: File name without extension, in uppercase

options.help: Accepted and ignored.
Folder of the hardware database. Otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

examples.title: Disk with one program
examples.cmd: vcc disk d64 -o game.d64 --name GAME --id 01 --add jumprun.prg:JUMPRUN

notes: The output shows the size and the free blocks.

Accepted, but has no effect on ATR images.
Accepted and ignored.
Folder of the hardware database. Otherwise VC_DATA or next to the program.

examples.title: ATR with one file as AUTORUN.SYS

notes: The image is 90 KB (720 sectors of 128 bytes). The form `atr-boot` creates a bootable disk without a file system.

forms.summary: Create a bootable ATR disk from an XEX program

options.help: Output file of the image.
XEX program that the disk loads at power-on (boot loader from the hardware database).
Folder of the hardware database. It provides the boot loader.

notes: `--boot` cannot be combined with `--add`: the boot disk has no file system. `vcc disk list` reports this.
A file without an XEX signature ($FFFF at the start) causes an error.

forms.summary: Change an existing ATR image (replace, delete and add files)

options.help: Output file of the image (not the base image).
Base image (ATR, DOS 2); it stays unchanged, the result goes to the output file.
Add a file or replace it, optionally under a different name.
Delete a file from the disk (its sectors become free).
Add a file; if the name already exists, that is an error.
Write-protected files may be deleted with --delete.
Accepted and ignored.

examples.title: Reduce the base image
examples.cmd: vcc disk atr -o new.atr --base turbo.atr --delete COMPILER.COM --delete RUNTIME.COM --force

notes: Write-protected files (`*` in vcc disk list) can only be deleted with --force and --put never overwrites them. The image is checked afterwards; on errors no output file is written.
The output shows the size and the free sectors. For Turbo BASIC XL projects see vcc turbo.

forms.summary: Show and check the directory of an image

args.name: image
args.help: Disk image. The extension (d64, d71, d81, atr) sets the format.

notes: Commodore: block count, name, file type and free blocks. Atari: name, sectors, start sector, `*` for protected files, and free sectors.
The check (BAM or VTOC, directory, file chains) reports differences as "Problem:" on stderr.

exit.1: file not readable or problem found in the image

forms.summary: Extract a file from an image

args.name: image
args.help: Disk image. The extension sets the format.

options.help: Target file.
options.default_text: Commodore: NAME in lowercase with extension .prg; Atari: NAME in lowercase

examples.title: Extract a program from a D64
examples.cmd: vcc disk extract game.d64 JUMPRUN -o jumprun.prg

examples.title: Extract a file from an ATR
examples.cmd: vcc disk extract game.atr AUTORUN.SYS -o autorun.sys
